issue.title: [nav2_behavior_tree] TruncatePathLocal action uses robot base frame id only from input port and not from parameter file
issue.body:
## Bug report

The TruncatePathLocal action only uses the robot base frame id from the input port instead of considering the corresponding global parameter. Furthermore, the input port does not use the default convention `robot_base_frame` and is named `robot_frame` instead.


#### Steps to reproduce issue

Use a setup where the base frame id is different to `base_link`. Set the frame id correctly in the parameter file, e.g. `robot_base_frame: my_fancy_robot/base_link`. All standard plugins will use the correct frame id. However, TruncatePathLocal will fail to get the corresponding transform with the following error:

```
[bt_navigator-4] [ERROR] [1782284475.666245003] [transformPoseInTargetFrame]: No Transform available Error looking up target frame: "base_link" passed to lookupTransform argument source_frame does not exist. 
[bt_navigator-4] 
[bt_navigator-4] [WARN] [1782284475.666302098] [my_fancy_robot.bt_navigator_navigate_to_pose_rclcpp_node]: Failed to lookup current robot pose for TruncatePathLocal
```

#### Expected behavior

The plugin should use the robot base frame id from the parameter file when the input port is not set. Furthermore, the parameter should be named according to the convention `robot_base_frame`.


#### Actual behavior

Only uses the value from the input port and the parameter is named `robot_frame`.

#### Reproduction instructions

See above.

#### Additional information

I suggest the following changes.

`truncate_path_local_action.hpp`:
```diff
--- a/truncate_path_local_action.hpp	2026-06-24 10:07:10.783801889 +0200
+++ b/truncate_path_local_action.hpp	2026-06-24 11:23:58.999565137 +0200
@@ -38,7 +38,7 @@
  * Usage in XML:
  * @code
  * <TruncatePathLocal input_path="{path}" output_path="{path_local}"
- *                    distance_forward="3.5" distance_backward="2.0" robot_frame="base_link"/>
+ *                    distance_forward="3.5" distance_backward="2.0" />
  * @endcode
  */
 class TruncatePathLocal : public BT::ActionNodeBase
@@ -74,7 +74,7 @@
         "distance_backward", 4.0,
         "Distance in backward direction"),
       BT::InputPort<std::string>(
-        "robot_frame", "base_link",
+        "robot_base_frame",
         "Robot base frame id"),
       BT::InputPort<double>(
         "transform_tolerance", 0.2,
```

`truncate_path_local_action.cpp`:
```diff
--- a/truncate_path_local_action.cpp	2026-06-24 10:07:24.086147245 +0200
+++ b/truncate_path_local_action.cpp	2026-06-24 11:26:23.200461096 +0200
@@ -116,11 +116,13 @@
   std::string path_frame_id, geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped & pose)
 {
   if (!getInput("pose", pose)) {
-    std::string robot_frame;
-    if (!getInput("robot_frame", robot_frame)) {
+    auto node = config().blackboard->get<nav2::LifecycleNode::SharedPtr>("node");
+    std::string robot_frame = BT::deconflictPortAndParamFrame<std::string>(
+      node, "robot_base_frame", this);;
+    if (robot_frame.empty()) {
       RCLCPP_ERROR(
-        config().blackboard->get<nav2::LifecycleNode::SharedPtr>("node")->get_logger(),
-        "Neither pose nor robot_frame specified for %s", name().c_str());
+        node->get_logger(),
+        "Neither pose nor robot_base_frame specified for %s", name().c_str());
       return false;
     }
     double transform_tolerance;
@@ -129,7 +131,7 @@
         pose, *tf_buffer_, path_frame_id, robot_frame, transform_tolerance))
     {
       RCLCPP_WARN(
-        config().blackboard->get<nav2::LifecycleNode::SharedPtr>("node")->get_logger(),
+        node->get_logger(),
         "Failed to lookup current robot pose for %s", name().c_str());
       return false;
     }
```

comments.body:
Hey @JoachimClemens, I came across this same issue while working on a project with a custom robot frame. Saw your issue and the suggested fix, waited a few days in case you were planning to submit the PR but figured I'd go ahead and implement it since the fix was well defined.

PR #6242 followed your suggested approach with [deconflictPortAndParamFrame()](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/AdilFarooq/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/4fe60c8b1c/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) and renamed the port to robot_base_frame. Also added a test case to catch the regression.

Thanks for reporting the bug and outlining the solution it made the fix straightforward.
